method: Every Scribe sentence with speech is labelled (437 of 437, 7.8 s - 1487.3 s): subscribe voice-over, the Himalaya ad read, Keerthi's clinic (Aravind begs for Hamsini's past), the Soham/Keerthi phone call, the scooty and street breakup flashback, the B&W echo, the dental clinic (Soham with a woman and girl, the receptionist), the B&W memory of Keerthi, the café (Aravind's rant, Keerthi's hospital call), the night at home (Hamsini and her mother: Aravind topic, wine, 'call me పద్దు', the advice, 'for suppose'), Aravind at the mother's house (B&W flash of her shouting, coffee, apology, beard banter, 'All the best'), and the school steps (cliffhanger 'Soham చనిపోయాడురా!'). Lines are Scribe sentences, unmerged and unsplit. For each line 5 frames evenly spaced over the line (lines under 1.2 s padded by 0.25 s each side) were taken from a 6 fps decode of the video and stacked into one strip per line: runs/gt/epZ0lbXkgWA/frames_key/line_<start seconds>.jpg (e.g. line_0017.82.jpg). Each strip was checked for who is on screen and whose mouth moves, combined with content (names and forms of address such as 'అమ్మా', 'బాబు', 'bro', 'madam', 'కీర్తి', 'సోహం', who answers whom, story logic). Short or doubtful lines between male and female voices were cross-checked with a median-F0 autocorrelation pitch estimate on the episode audio (Aravind ~110-130 Hz, the women ~250-300 Hz), noted on the line. Speaker decided from frames and content before looking at Scribe labels; Scribe label (majority word speaker, ties by overlap seconds, as eval.speakers.line_label) and its time share added afterwards. Character names come only from what is said in this episode (no on-screen name cards: the opening has location-courtesy and subscribe cards, the 8:52-9:00 card is the series title 'Hello Madam 2', and the end credits list crew/cast without character names); actors' names from the YouTube description were not used. Pipeline outputs (runs/name_test, runs/selection_v2, runs/speaker_fix, runs/asr_fix, data/series_cast, data/gold) were not opened.

label_conventions.speaker: character name from the list; 'OFFSCREEN:<name>' = the speaker is not visible during the line (reaction shot held on a listener, insert shot, memory/echo voice-over) but is identified from content/voice context; 'UNKNOWN' = cannot tell. For diarization scoring, strip the OFFSCREEN: prefix. In this key OFFSCREEN is also used when the shot is held on a listener and only the speaker's blurred head/shoulder/back is at the frame edge (listed in on_screen_partly); a speaker filmed from behind as the subject of the shot keeps the plain name. Inner-thought voice-over by a visible character keeps the plain name (note says so).
label_conventions.confidence: 3 = seen speaking and/or unambiguous from content; 2 = likely (wide shot, back to camera or cut mid-line, content supports); 1 = guess
label_conventions.times: seconds in the episode audio; keyed by time, not by Scribe line id
label_conventions.on_screen: everyone visible at any moment during the line (union over the line's frames); [] = nobody (an insert shot such as a pan on the stove); on_screen_partly = only a back / shoulder / chest is visible. Independent of speaker: the speaker may be off screen while others are shown. Lines without on_screen are not scored for it. Background extras (passers-by at the school) are not listed.
label_conventions.voices: only on lines with more than one voice: a list in time order of {from_text: the first word of that voice's part, copied from the line's text, speakers: [names]}; two people one after another = two entries; several people saying it together = one entry with several names. Lines without voices were checked and have a single voice (clip-gt-editor 2026-11-02: Scribe word speakers inside the line, content, frames; no line in this key needed it — back-to-back interjections are already separate Scribe sentences, e.g. 24:08.41 / 24:08.47).
label_conventions.on_screen_founder: Founder 2026-11-03: a character filmed from behind (back of the head / shoulder in an over-the-shoulder shot) is in the frame; the founder's corrections count them as on screen.
